why: rate limiting is a dependency: attach Depends in add_api_route, stored on APIRoute, resolved per-request by solve_dependencies building a Dependant graph
the @app.exception_handler decorator registers the handler; the handler switches on the exception types you'd override (HTTPException, RequestValidationError)
the @app.websocket decorator and its registrar build an APIWebSocketRoute; the websocket route class is the endpoint's wrapper

task: include a sub-router with a URL prefix
why: app.include_router(router, prefix=...) is how a sub-router is mounted; both APIRouter.include_router and FastAPI.include_router accept the router + prefix, and APIRouter is the sub-router class
@app.middleware('http') wraps a dispatch function; build_middleware_stack is where the ASGI stack is assembled

task: make a POST request with a JSON body
why: httpx.post delegates to httpx.request; the Request model holds json=content, Response is the returned object
subclass Auth (auth_flow) for custom auth; BasicAuth is the reference impl; Client applies auth per request via _build_auth

task: set a timeout and connection limits
why: Timeout and Limits are the config objects; Client.__init__ accepts timeout=/limits= and threads them into the transport
httpx.stream and Client.stream are the streaming entry points; Response.iter_bytes is the body iterator used for large responses

task: use a mock transport in tests
why: MockTransport implements a handler transport; BaseTransport is its base class; Client._init_transport adopts a passed transport= in __init__
